conviction_note: The findings sum to -1.3 and the scaled number is -0.8 (p_up 42 x abs_move 5.0). The main fact comes from the company's own documents: the Dallas office loan was repaid at a $1.5M discount (8-K, 5 Oct), and SEVN's own definition charges realized losses to distributable earnings (DE) at repayment. That cuts about $0.067/sh from a Q3 DE guide of $0.23-0.25, which was set while management said the loan would pay off. It is a one-off already covered by a $6.3M reserve, and GAAP net income gets a reserve release, so it is sized small. p_up stays only mildly below 50 because the stock already yields ~17.8% at a 52-week low.

findings.finding: The Dallas office loan ($44.2M principal, risk-rated 4, $6.3M CECL reserve at 6/30) was repaid at about 97% of balance in Q3, with a ~$1.5M discount. SEVN's own DE definition says DE is 'reduced for realized losses on loan investments when amounts are deemed uncollectable ... generally at the time a loan is repaid'. That is about $0.067/sh off DE on 22.4M shares, so reported Q3 DE would land near $0.16-0.19 against the company's $0.23-0.25 guide (the guide was given when management said 'We believe that loan will be paid off' and that the appraisal covered it). The same event releases most of the $6.3M reserve (~$4.8M, ~$0.21/sh) into GAAP net income, so GAAP EPS likely beats while headline DE misses. Net sign negative because this name trades on DE against the $0.28 dividend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: DE $0.23 against $0.25 consensus and at the low end of the guide; stock -4.73% on the print (baseline) and -4.7% to $7.66 per Simply Wall St. 5 of the last 7 prints were negative. The 2026-10-05 release disclosing the discount traded +1.3% (6.75 -> 6.84), so the market read it as de-risking, not as a DE hit.
findings.why_not_priced: The discount is public but was never stated in DE terms: the 10-05 release gives no earnings figure and no sell-side Q3 DE number is visible. If the market had mapped it into DE, the 10-05 session would not have closed up, and the Q3 guide would have been visibly reset. This is a first-ever realized loss ('no realized losses to date' through Q2), so there is no precedent for how SEVN presents it. They may headline DE before realized losses, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: The DE definition (realized losses reduce DE at repayment) is in a different document, the Q2 2026 earnings presentation: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1452477/000145247726000028/sevnq22026earningspresen.htm . Loan #2 Dallas, $44.2M, risk 4, maturity 2026-08-25. Office exposure falling from 19% to ~13% by 9/30 confirms the repayment fell in Q3.

findings.finding: Arithmetic from company documents suggests the year-end portfolio target and with it 'dividend coverage by year end' will slip. The target is $950-960M (Q2 call). 6/30 principal was $722.3M. Since then: +$24.3M July loan, +$98.0M two loans announced 10-05, -$44.2M Dallas, -$25.3M Fayetteville, +$121.7M in diligence for Q4, and a Carlsbad $24.5M office repayment expected in Q4. That gives roughly $870-900M before future fundings, about $60-90M short. Q3 DE also loses the reduced-NIM office and storage loans only near quarter end. On the call the coverage timeline is likely to move into 2027, against management's 'committed to this dividend level through 2026 at a minimum'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 call kept coverage 'by year end' and the stock still fell -4.7% on a DE miss. July 2025: a 20% dividend cut (0.35 -> 0.28) traded -2.9% pre-market (https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/seven-hills-realty-trust-stock-falls-after-reducing-quarterly-dividend-93CH-2001326).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a 17.8% yield ($1.12 on $6.29) already discounts a cut, and the stock is 3.6% above its 52-week low. What is not public is management's own revised year-end portfolio and coverage date. If that were known, the 10-08 $0.28 declaration would not have been the last word on the dividend. The arithmetic is my inference and the company has not confirmed it.
findings.independence: Shares source data with the 10-05 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1452477/000110465926113721/tm2627052d1_ex99-1.htm) and the Q2 presentation for the 6/30 principal. It is an inference, not a company statement.

findings.finding: Carlsbad, CA office loan ($24.5M principal, $24.75M committed, risk-rated 4, part of the reserve build on 'two office loans with 2026 maturities') matures 2026-10-27, the print date. The 10-05 release expects a Q4 repayment and gives no amount. A discount like Dallas's would be a second realized loss of roughly $0.03-0.05/sh in Q4 DE; a par repayment would release reserve. The call will likely say which.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior realized loss on SEVN. The Dallas resolution (10-05) traded +1.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The repayment terms are unannounced. A priced discount would show as the stock trading at or below a reserve-adjusted book, which cannot be checked without the Q3 book value.
findings.independence: The 10-05 8-K separately confirms the expected Q4 Carlsbad repayment: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1452477/000110465926113721/tm2627052d1_ex99-1.htm

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the fed funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16. SEVN is a floating-rate first-mortgage lender at 1.5x debt/equity, so roughly $270M of net floating exposure gains about $0.7M a year, about $0.008/sh a quarter. That is a small tailwind to Q4 DE and to the coverage path. Higher rates also stress transitional-CRE borrowers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SEVN cut its dividend in July 2025 citing a falling SOFR curve (https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/seven-hills-realty-trust-stock-falls-after-reducing-quarterly-dividend-93CH-2001326), so the company itself ties rates to coverage.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro is public. This is a proxy until management quantifies the effect in the Q4 outlook. The stock fell after the hike (-4.7% on 9-30), so the market is reading the credit side, not the income side.
